title: Character registry (authority file), version 1
description: One entry per character. The only place a canonical name is written. Every other file references or is checked against it. Procedure: ~/.agents/skills/character-registry-ssot/SKILL.md

visual_continuity.description: Path of the visual-continuity manifest, relative to this file. Its stories' scenes_file and continuity_file become surfaces.

skip_stories.description: Manifest stories whose files are not surfaces, each with the reason (a fixture, a placeholder cast).

root.description: scenes: the key holding the scene map (default scenes).

fields.description: scenes: label fields (default characters, speaker, marginAuthor, dialogue[].speaker).

paths.description: names: dot paths with * and [] wildcards whose string values are labels.

split.description: Extra separators for compound labels (default &, +, and).

pattern.description: headings: a regex whose first group is the label (default ### headings up to the first parenthesis).

within.description: headings: only lines after this exact heading line, up to the next heading of the same level.

prose.description: scenes: scan every string of each scene for retired names (default true).

ignore.description: headings: exact heading labels that are not characters (a timeline, a table) and are skipped.

story_field.description: prose: the field of each entry under root whose value picks the story through `stories` (default: the entry's key).

stories.description: prose: map from a story_field value (or entry key) to a story id; an entry whose value is not mapped is skipped.

skip_keys.description: prose and continuity: keys whose strings are not scanned, besides every key starting with _ (notes and sources).

kind.description: person; companion (an animal or a named companion object: a dog, a cat, a plush bear); voice (a device or document that speaks); group (members listed).

story.description: Home story id (a visual-continuity story id, or any label such as moment-packs or platform).

also_in.description: Other story ids this character may appear in; "*" means every story.

role.description: One line. The profile holds the rest.

aliases.description: Every other label a surface uses for this character. Exact strings.

retired.description: Forms that may never return. A label equal to one, or a scene string containing one, fails.

first_appearance.description: A scene slug in the home story.

ages.description: Stated age anchors by year; checked against born.

continuity_ids.description: Keys in the home story's continuity file characters block.

sources.description: Files that describe this character, relative to the registry; a #fragment may follow the path.

questions.description: Open questions about this character that block nothing: a shared surname, a name an agent chose, a date to settle. Each line says who raised it and when. The owner answers them when he wants to; nothing waits on them.

prose_only.description: True when this character is named only inside prose, never on a label field, so the check does not report a gap.

species.description: companion: a key of the registry's species map (required for every companion).

generic.description: True for a descriptive label standing in for an unnamed person (The therapist, Diner Manager): it is a label on its surfaces but is not hunted for in other stories' prose.

full_name.description: The full form a {{id:full}} token renders (Chloe Jenkins) when the canonical name is shorter (Chloe).

forms.description: Named forms a {{id:<form>}} token renders (formal: Samantha, full: Samantha Hayes, surname: Hayes). A form here overrides the built-ins first, short, full, initial.

records.description: Globs (relative to this file; ** and * as in gitignore) of dated history that is never rewritten: the worklog, transcripts, decision records, research, past prompt records, retired plans, test fixtures. Every other tracked text file is scanned for retired names and companion species mismatches.

species.description: Species a companion may have, each with the words that name it in prose (nouns only; never a word that is also a verb). A story's text may name only the species of companions allowed in that story.

known.description: Problems the gate reports as gaps instead of failures while another lane or the owner resolves them: the file, a substring of the problem line, who owns it, the worklog task and the date.

token_sources.description: Files that write no character's name (ADR-014): they hold {{id}} tokens and a builder renders the names. Scene files, cards and prose surfaces are token sources already; list the rest (pages, partials, manifests, records a builder reads) here, as a path or a glob.

skip_keys.description: Keys whose strings are not checked: a label the file defines, printed text of a physical object, a dated note.
